title: Skala option registry
description: The single source of truth for every style option Skala knows about. docs/plan/03-configuration-model.md § "The option registry".

valueAliases.description: ReSharper's alternative spellings for a value, e.g. true -> always.

key.description: The canonical .editorconfig spelling, verbatim. Skala's own namespace (`skala_`), or the standard EditorConfig/Microsoft spelling where the option is Microsoft's.

aliases.description: Every other spelling Skala accepts for this one option. An alias that reaches two options is SK9004. ⚠ ReSharper's spellings are NOT aliases — see `export`.

export.description: The spelling(s) the Rider export (`editor_config_template`) uses for this option. ⚠ Provenance only: never indexed by `OptionRegistry.TryResolve`, so a `resharper_*` key in a user's .editorconfig is an unknown key (SK9001). `CanonicalEditorConfig.Compose` translates the export into Skala's namespace through this, and `EditorConfigIngestionTests` uses it to state that Skala's own configuration says what the export says.

type.description: bool | int | string | enum:<Name> | flags:<Name>, where <Name> is a key of `enums`. `string` means every string is legal, which is a claim about the option and not a shrug: an entry may only carry it together with `freeFormBecause`, and OptionValueValidationTests asserts the exemption list against the registry.

min.description: For an int, the smallest value the option accepts, inclusive. Omit where no lower bound is knowable; a missing bound is better than a guessed one. ⚠ Read it together with the clamping the consumer does — `max_line_length = 0` and `skala_max_invocation_arguments_on_line = 0` are values the formatter deliberately supports (0 means 'the default width' and 'chop always'), so their minimum is 0 and not 1.

max.description: For an int, the largest value the option accepts, inclusive. Almost always absent: an upper bound nobody can justify is a value refused for no reason.

boundsBecause.description: Required whenever `min` or `max` is set, and forbidden otherwise: why that bound is knowable. A bound with no reason is the same guess the missing bound was, written down more confidently.

tabMeans.description: The key whose value the literal `tab` stands for. Set on `indent_size` only, because the EditorConfig specification defines the alias there and nowhere else.

freeFormBecause.description: Required on, and only on, a `string` entry: why this option has no closed domain. A `string` with no reason is how 27 options that are really enums came to accept anything at all — the reason is what makes the next reader able to challenge it.

inert.description: Why no input can distinguish this option's values — another rule wins by the documented ordering, the writer cannot produce the shape it governs, or the export's own value of a named key masks it. A claim about the world, so it must be established with a probe and it must name the probe. Tier D only: OptionRegistryTests forbids the pair with any other tier, because an inert option that claimed Tier A would mean a fixture pinning behaviour no input can produce.

unsweptBecause.description: Why this entry names no `oracle` fixture, when `inert` is not the answer — the two are different claims and merging them is how a real gap gets filed as a vacuous one. `inert` says nothing can distinguish the values; this says the SWEEP cannot ask. Usually that is a fact about Skala rather than about the option: the oracle separates the values and Skala is flat at every one, so a glob would file an INERT row the registry never declared, on a fixture Skala cannot reproduce. It is also where a Tier C refusal's measurement goes, since `inert` is Tier D by construction. Forbidden together with `inert`, and forbidden on an entry that has an `oracle`.

default.description: ReSharper's default for this option, in its .editorconfig spelling. Read together with defaultSource: it is only trustworthy when defaultSource is resharper-docs.

defaultSource.description: Where `default` came from. resharper-docs: verified against JetBrains' published property tables. oracle-probe: derived by running jb cleanupcode under a configuration carrying nothing but root = true and comparing against the fixture that exercises the option — a strong signal rather than proof, because options interact. template: the value the Rider export holds, which is Rider's default for most keys and the author's choice for the rest, with nothing distinguishing the two. unknown: no basis beyond the export. `skala config distill` may only drop a key when this is resharper-docs or oracle-probe.

tier.description: docs/plan/03 § "Four tiers". A: implemented and pinned by an oracle fixture. B: approximated, with a documented divergence. C: accepted and deliberately ignored. D: known but not implemented.

templateLine.description: The line in editor_config_template this entry was seeded from. Provenance only.

severitySuffix.description: True for Microsoft style keys written as value:severity.

expands.description: For one of ReSharper's generalized properties, the options it sets at once.
